cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to explain to you the differences between three different terms that are often used together.
cues.zh: 這部影片，要解釋三個經常一起使用的術語有何不同。

cues.en: And these are terms that are important for not only for statistics, but also just for measurement in science more generally.
cues.zh: 它們不只對統計重要，對更一般的科學測量也重要。

cues.en: So the terms are accuracy, precision, and resolution.
cues.zh: 也就是準確度、精密度與解析度。

cues.en: These terms are sometimes used interchangeably, but that's not really accurate.
cues.zh: 有時會混用這些詞，但那其實不準確。

cues.en: These are separate concepts, although they're all equally important for doing good high quality science and statistical analyses.
cues.zh: 它們是不同概念，雖然對高品質科學與統計分析，都同樣重要。

cues.en: So I'm gonna begin with some definitions of each of these, and then I'll show you in some graphical examples how they're related to each other.
cues.zh: 先定義各個術語，再用圖例展示彼此關係。

cues.en: So accuracy we can say is the relationship between the measurement, so the numbers coming out of your measurement sensors,
cues.zh: 準確度，可以說是測量值，也就是測量感測器輸出的數字，

cues.en: whether that's a self-report questionnaire or an electrode
cues.zh: 不論是自陳問卷、電極，

cues.en: or a pixel in a camera.
cues.zh: 或相機的像素，

cues.en: So the relationship between the measurement and the actual truth, the thing that's really out there in the universe, in the real world, this is, so accuracy is inversely related to bias.
cues.zh: 與真實情況，也就是宇宙、真實世界中實際存在事物的關係。準確度與偏差呈反向關係。

cues.en: So sometimes you'll hear people use the term bias instead of accuracy, and that's fine.
cues.zh: 所以有時會聽到人們用偏差代替準確度，也沒問題。

cues.en: So accuracy, I think is the more kind of established term.
cues.zh: 我認為準確度是更通行的術語。

cues.en: And bias is also possible.
cues.zh: 也可以用偏差。

cues.en: So if you have a measurement bias, then your measurement is not so accurate.
cues.zh: 如果有測量偏差，測量就不太準確。

cues.en: Okay and then the next term is precision.
cues.zh: 下一個術語是精密度。

cues.en: And the precision is related to the certainty of each measurement.
cues.zh: 精密度與每次測量的確定程度有關。

cues.en: So you can imagine if you have so let's imagine you have a camera and you take a picture of the world.
cues.zh: 想像有一台相機，對世界拍照。

cues.en: Let's say you have the camera on a stand so that you're not moving, the camera isn't moving.
cues.zh: 把相機放在架子上，你沒有動，相機也沒動。

cues.en: And let's say you're taking a picture of the mountain.
cues.zh: 假設拍攝一座山。

cues.en: So the mountain isn't really appreciably moving either.
cues.zh: 山也沒有明顯移動。

cues.en: Let's imagine that each time you take a picture of the same mountain with the camera in the same position, the picture looks different.
cues.zh: 想像相機在同一位置，每次拍同一座山，照片卻都不同。

cues.en: Maybe the the light levels are different, or the granularity is different, then we could say that the camera doesn't have very high precision.
cues.zh: 可能亮度不同，或顆粒感不同，就能說相機精密度不高。

cues.en: The precision is low if the measurement changes each time you remeasure the same device.
cues.zh: 每次對同一個對象重複測量，結果都改變，就是精密度低。

cues.en: Conversely, modern cameras are actually quite precise.
cues.zh: 相反地，現代相機其實很精密。

cues.en: So you know, nowadays when you take if you take three pictures of the same mountain without the camera moving, then those three pictures are going to look really, really, really similar.
cues.zh: 現在相機不動，對同一座山拍三張照片，三張會非常非常相似。

cues.en: So modern cameras are very precise.
cues.zh: 所以現代相機很精密。

cues.en: You can be confident that when you take one measurement, another measurement of the, you know, another repetition of the same measurement is going to look really, really similar.
cues.zh: 測量一次，就能有信心，再重複相同測量，結果會非常相似。

cues.en: So that's high precision.
cues.zh: 這是高精密度。

cues.en: This is also inversely related to variance.
cues.zh: 它也與變異數呈反向關係。

cues.en: So if your measurement has a lot of variance, then it has low precision.
cues.zh: 測量變異數很大，精密度就低。

cues.en: Again, precision is a more established term in statistics and in scientific measurement theory and variants to be used in this sense
cues.zh: 同樣，精密度在統計與科學測量理論中，是較通行的術語。把變異數用在這種意義，

cues.en: is somewhat less common because mostly people using variance to describe the dispersion of data across different samples from different individuals.
cues.zh: 比較不常見，因為大家主要用變異數描述不同個體、不同樣本之間，資料的離散程度。

cues.en: So we'll talk more about that in a few videos.
cues.zh: 再過幾部影片會深入討論。

cues.en: Okay, so accuracy, precision.
cues.zh: 以上是準確度與精密度。

cues.en: The last term here is resolution.
cues.zh: 最後是解析度。

cues.en: And resolution is the number of data points per unit measurement.
cues.zh: 解析度，是每單位測量中資料點的數量。

cues.en: So if you're measuring signals over time, then you're going to sample at some number of time points.
cues.zh: 如果隨時間測量訊號，就會在若干時間點取樣。

cues.en: Let's say you're measuring at 100 hertz, that means you're taking 100 measurements in each second.
cues.zh: 假設以100赫茲測量，代表每秒測100次。

cues.en: So then the resolution is 100 hertz.
cues.zh: 所以解析度是100赫茲。

cues.en: If you're measuring something over space, we can think about this again, using the example of cameras.
cues.zh: 如果測量空間中的東西，再用相機當例子。

cues.en: You can have a camera that has higher resolution or lower resolution.
cues.zh: 相機可以有較高或較低的解析度。

cues.en: And what does that mean?
cues.zh: 代表什麼？

cues.en: The total amount of space that the lens is sensitive to is the same, but when you have more pixels, you have higher resolution.
cues.zh: 鏡頭感應的總空間相同，但像素越多，解析度越高。

cues.en: So a high resolution camera has more pixels for the same unit area compared to a lower resolution camera.
cues.zh: 所以相同單位面積，高解析度相機的像素，比低解析度相機多。

cues.en: Okay so what I'm gonna do now is show you this picture.
cues.zh: 現在展示這張圖。

cues.en: It's a bullseye.
cues.zh: 這是靶心。

cues.en: And the idea is that a bullseye is the thing in the universe that we are trying to measure.
cues.zh: 概念是，靶心代表宇宙中，我們想測量的事物。

cues.en: So we wanna measure from, you know, we wanna measure at the bullseye, and each one of these black dots corresponds to an actual measurement.
cues.zh: 想測量靶心，每個黑點，對應一次實際測量。

cues.en: This is a data point that we have measured.
cues.zh: 這是一個已測量的資料點。

cues.en: So the R is for resolution, P is for precision, A is for accuracy.
cues.zh: R代表解析度，P代表精密度，A代表準確度。

cues.en: And basically these different graphs here are illustrating different ways of combining resolution, precision, and accuracy.
cues.zh: 這些不同圖，展示解析度、精密度與準確度的不同組合。

cues.en: So here we have high resolution because there's a lot of dots.
cues.zh: 這裡解析度高，因為很多點。

cues.en: So a lot is a relative term, but you know, relative to three dots.
cues.zh: 很多是相對的，但相較三個點而言，

cues.en: So we have a lot of dots, so that's high resolution.
cues.zh: 有很多點，所以解析度高。

cues.en: We have high precision because all the dots are really similar to each other.
cues.zh: 精密度高，因為所有點都很接近。

cues.en: So each time we measure this system over and over again, we can be pretty confident that we are getting the same result again and again.
cues.zh: 每次反覆測量這個系統，都能相當有信心，結果會一再相同。

cues.en: However, the accuracy is actually very low, right?
cues.zh: 但準確度其實非常低，對吧？

cues.en: We should be measuring right here at the bullseye, but we're not.
cues.zh: 應該量到這裡的靶心，但沒有。

cues.en: There is a bias.
cues.zh: 存在偏差。

cues.en: So the accuracy is low.
cues.zh: 所以準確度低。

cues.en: Here's the same thing, but now the accuracy is high.
cues.zh: 這裡情況相同，但準確度高。

cues.en: This is kind of an ideal scenario, right?
cues.zh: 這有點像理想情況。

cues.en: You have high resolution, high precision, and high accuracy.
cues.zh: 高解析度、高精密度、高準確度。

cues.en: All of your sensor bullet point measurements are really close to the origin of this bullseye.
cues.zh: 所有感測器測量點，都很接近這個靶心的中心。

cues.en: So, and so, this is like an ideal scenario.
cues.zh: 所以這是理想情況。

cues.en: This is a not a really great scenario.
cues.zh: 這則不是很好的情況。

cues.en: Here we have low resolution, we don't have a lot of data points.
cues.zh: 解析度低，資料點不多。

cues.en: We have low accuracy because we're not getting the bullseye.
cues.zh: 準確度低，因為沒命中靶心。

cues.en: And we also have low precision because each measurement is really far apart from every other measurement.
cues.zh: 精密度也低，因為每次測量都與其他測量相隔很遠。

cues.en: So if you get one measurement here, you're not really sure where the other measurements are going to be.
cues.zh: 在這裡得到一個測量，也不確定其他測量會在哪裡。

cues.en: They could also be here.
cues.zh: 可能在這裡。

cues.en: They could be here, or here or here.
cues.zh: 可能在這裡、這裡，或這裡。

cues.en: So the precision is fairly low. Okay?
cues.zh: 所以精密度相當低，好嗎？

cues.en: So there's many several more of these.
cues.zh: 這裡還有好幾個。

cues.en: I'll just go through this one because this is also pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 只再看這個，因為也很有意思。

cues.en: So here the resolution is high. We have a lot of dots.
cues.zh: 這裡解析度高，很多點。

cues.en: The accuracy is actually pretty high because we are, you know, you can see the center of this cluster of measurements is pretty close to the bullseye where we want to be measuring,
cues.zh: 準確度其實相當高，因為這群測量值的中心，很接近想測的靶心，

cues.en: but the precision is low.
cues.zh: 但精密度低。

cues.en: So this is actually a fairly common situation in empirical science, particularly in biology, neuroscience, psychology.
cues.zh: 這其實是實證科學，尤其生物學、神經科學與心理學，常見的情況。

cues.en: We might have very accurate measurements, but our measurements are fairly noisy.
cues.zh: 測量可能非常準確，但含有不少雜訊。

cues.en: So we have to acquire a lot of data.
cues.zh: 所以必須取得大量資料。

cues.en: And the idea is that the more data we can acquire, the more of these measurement points we can average over.
cues.zh: 概念是，資料越多，能用來平均的測量點越多。

cues.en: And you can see that as we average over more and more data points, we're gonna get closer.
cues.zh: 可以看到，平均的資料點越多，就會越接近。

cues.en: The average of all these sensor measurements is gonna get closer and closer to the correct answer, and that's because we have high accuracy.
cues.zh: 所有感測器測量的平均，會越接近正確答案，因為準確度高。

cues.en: All right?
cues.zh: 明白嗎？

cues.en: So if you like, you can pause the video, make sure you understand these two bullseye as well.
cues.zh: 如果願意，可以暫停，確保也理解另外兩張靶心圖。

cues.en: I hope you now understand the distinctions between accuracy, precision, and resolution.
cues.zh: 希望現在理解準確度、精密度與解析度的差別。

cues.en: Again, these are distinct but related concepts that are all important for empirical sciences and statistics.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，它們是不同但相關的概念，對實證科學與統計都重要。
